title: Arakhin 26
description: Why Rabbi Eliezer holds that an unredeemed consecrated field never passes to the priests, how the verse’s “anymore” is read for a field the priests have already received, whether an owner who redeems in the second Jubilee cycle is “like another”, and a new mishna on a son who bought his father’s field.
topics: 🐑 Temple maintenance from Temple maintenance, priestly gifts from priestly gifts: the house and the Shavuot lambs

🧑‍🌾 After the priests: a priest who consecrates the field, a priest who sells it, and “to the one from whom it was bought”
🚪 Rava: “when it goes out” in the Jubilee, from the possession of another

a1.he: מִקׇּדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת, וְאֵין דָּנִין קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת מִקׇּדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ.

a2.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן נָמֵי, נֵילַף מִמַּקְדִּישׁ בַּיִת! דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁמַּתָּנָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, מִדָּבָר שֶׁמַּתָּנָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וְאֵין דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁמַּתָּנָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, מִדָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַתָּנָה לַכֹּהֲנִים.

a3.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא נִכְנָסִין, וְלֹא נוֹתְנִין.

a4.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר? אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִם לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד, וְאִם מָכַר אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל״.

a5.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סַכִּינָא חֲרִיפָא מַפְסְקָא קְרָאֵי? אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כִּדְתַנְיָא: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״עוֹד״ — לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.

a6.he: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹבֵל רִאשׁוֹן — אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת? שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה נָמֵי הָוְיָא! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי.

a7.he: וּלְמַאן? אִילֵימָא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, לְכֹהֲנִים נָפְקָא! אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מֵהָכָא.

a8.he: וְתִסְבְּרָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי ״עוֹד״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ? אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּשָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ כֹּהֵן, וְאָתוּ בְּעָלִים לְמִיפְרְקַהּ.

a9.he: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: לָא תִּיפְרוֹק, שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה — תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עוֹד״, לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.

a10.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: ״בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״, יָכוֹל יַחְזוֹר לַגִּזְבָּר שֶׁלְּקָחוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ״.

a11.he: יֵאָמֵר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ״, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״? שָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצָאת לַכֹּהֲנִים, וּמְכָרָהּ כֹּהֵן, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ לוֹקֵחַ, וּגְאָלָהּ אַחֵר — יָכוֹל תַּחְזוֹר לַבְּעָלִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.

a13.he: דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, דְּלָא קָא הָדְרָה כְּלָל, אֲבָל הָכָא דְּקָא הָדְרָה, תִּיהְדַּר לְמָרַהּ קַמָּא, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.

a14.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״, דְּלָא קָא יָהֲבִי בְּעָלִים דָּמֵי, אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּקָא יָהֲבִי דְּמֵי, תֵּיקוּם בִּידַיְיהוּ, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״.

a15.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְלָא כְּתַב ״עוֹד״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: לָא תִּיפְרוֹק כְּלָל, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״עוֹד״, לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.

a16.he: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ? אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיּוֹבֵל״, בְּצֵאתוֹ מִיַּד אַחֵר.

b1.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי, כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ אוֹ לָא?

b2.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ — יָכוֹל לֹא תְּהֵא נִגְאֶלֶת, שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״עוֹד״ — לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.

b3.he: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא בְּיוֹבֵל רִאשׁוֹן — אַמַּאי אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת? אֲחוּזָּה נָמֵי הָוְיָא! אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי.

b4.he: וּלְמַאן? אִי לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — לְכֹהֲנִים נָפְקָא! אֶלָּא לָאו לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ.

b5.he: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ?! רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַאי ״עוֹד״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ? אֶלָּא, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? בְּשָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ כֹּהֵן, וַאֲתוֹ בְּעָלִים לְמִיפְרְקַהּ. סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: לָא תִּיפְרוֹק, שֶׁתְּהֵא כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה. תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עוֹד״ — לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.

b6.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: ״יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ״, יָכוֹל יַחְזוֹר לַגִּזְבָּר שֶׁלְּקָחָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לַאֲשֶׁר לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ״.

b7.he: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״? שָׂדֶה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים, וּמְכָרָהּ כֹּהֵן, וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ לוֹקֵחַ, וּגְאָלָהּ אַחֵר — יָכוֹל תַּחְזוֹר לַבְּעָלִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.

b8.he: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיכְתַּב ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיכְתַּב ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ דְּלָא קָא הָדְרָא כְּלָל, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״.

b9.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ״, דְּלָא קָיָהֲבִי בְּעָלִים דְּמֵי, אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּיָהֲבִי בְּעָלִים דְּמֵי, דְּתֵיקוּם בִּידַיְהוּ, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״.

b10.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״, וְלָא כְּתַב ״עוֹד״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לָא תִּיפְרוֹק כְּלָל, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״עוֹד״, לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהָיְתָה אֵינָהּ נִגְאֶלֶת, אֲבָל נִגְאֶלֶת שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָה.

b11.he: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ? תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: גְּאָלָהּ בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי — יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל.

b12.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הָאֲנַן לָא תְּנַן הָכִי, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין לְתוֹכָהּ עַד שֶׁיִּגְאָלֶנָּה אַחֵר! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ.

b13.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: גְּאָלָהּ בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי — אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים נִכְנָסִין לְתוֹכָהּ עַד שֶׁיִּגְאָלֶנָּה אַחֵר! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי מִמַּתְנִיתִין הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: בְּעָלִים בְּיוֹבֵל שֵׁנִי כְּאַחֵר דָּמוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

b14.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו, וּמֵת אָבִיו, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ — הֲרֵי הִיא כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה. הִקְדִּישָׁהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָבִיו — הֲרֵי הִיא כְּשָׂדֶה מִקְנָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.

b15.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים: הֲרֵי הִיא כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אִם מִשְּׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״, שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁהִיא רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.

b16.he: שְׂדֵה מִקְנָה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל, שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ. הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם מַקְדִּישִׁין לְעוֹלָם, וְגוֹאֲלִין לְעוֹלָם, בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל בֵּין לְאַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל.

b17.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו וְהִקְדִּישָׁהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מֵת אָבִיו, מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְאִם מִשְּׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״ — שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצְתָה זוֹ, שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.

b18.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לְלוֹקֵחַ שָׂדֶה מֵאָבִיו, וּמֵת אָבִיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְדִּישָׁהּ, מִנַּיִן שֶׁתְּהֵא לְפָנָיו כִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְאִם מִשְּׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״ — שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצָאת זוֹ שֶׁהִיא שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.

b19.he: לֵימָא בְּהָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.

b20.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבְרִי: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.

b21.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: בְּעָלְמָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי,

messages.text: Continued from 25b: if a consecrated ancestral field is not redeemed by the Jubilee, Rabbi Yehuda says the priests enter it and pay for it, deriving this from “holy” said of a consecrated house; Rabbi Shimon says they enter it without paying, deriving this from “holy” said of the two lambs of Shavuot. Asked why Rabbi Yehuda does not also derive from the lambs, the Gemara answered: one derives items consecrated for Temple maintenance, such as an ancestral field,

from that of other items consecrated for Temple maintenance, e.g., a consecrated house, but one does not derive the halakha with regard to items consecrated for Temple maintenance from items that are consecrated for the altar, such as the two lambs brought on Shavuot.
And let Rabbi Shimon also derive the halakha by means of a verbal analogy from one who consecrates a house. Why does he disagree with Rabbi Yehuda?

One derives the halakha of an item that is a gift to the priests, such as an ancestral field that is given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, from that of another item that is a gift to the priests, i.e., the two lambs brought on Shavuot, but one does not derive the halakha of an item that is a gift to the priests from that of an item that is not a gift to the priests, i.e., a consecrated house.

The priests do not enter into the field, and they also do not give its redemption payment to the Temple treasury. That is, the priests do not obtain possession of a consecrated field during the Jubilee Year unless another person redeemed it first.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that if one consecrates his ancestral field and it is not redeemed before the Jubilee,

messages.text: What is the reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion? It is because the verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed anymore. But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord, as a dedicated field; his ancestral possession shall be for the priest” (Leviticus 27:20–21).
messages.quote: The priests do not enter into the field

verse.he: וְאִם־לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה וְאִם־מָכַר אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד׃ וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: But if the one [who consecrated it] did not redeem the land, and the land was sold to another party, it shall no longer be redeemable: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.dh: רבי אלעזר אומר לא נכנסין ולא נותנין דמים להקדש אלא נקראת כו'
notes.he: מ"ט דרבי אלעזר אמר קרא אם לא יגאל את השדה. (עד) [קודם] שנת היובל לא יגאל עוד לבעלים אלא הרי היא של הקדש ולא נכנסין ולא נותנין דמים אבל אם מכר את השדה גזבר לאחר היובל לאחר אח"כ והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל לכהן תהיה:
notes.en: Rabbi Elazar says: They do not enter, and they do not give money to the Temple treasury; rather, it is called, etc. What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar? The verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field” [before] the Jubilee Year, “it shall not be redeemed anymore” by the owner; rather, it belongs to the Temple treasury, and [the priests] do not enter and do not give money. But “if he sold the field,” [that is, if] the treasurer [sold it] to another, after the Jubilee [comes] “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee,” shall be the priest’s. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads Rabbi Elazar throughout this discussion; the daf reads Rabbi Eliezer.]

messages.text: Rabbi Eliezer maintains that these verses teach two separate halakhot, and should be read as follows: “And if he will not redeem the field…it shall not be redeemed anymore,” as an ancestral field, and: “Or if he sold the field…But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee…his ancestral possession shall be for the priest.” Accordingly, if the field has not yet been sold to another man, it is not transferred to the priests during the Jubilee.

notes.he: מאי טעמא דרבי אליעזר אמר רבה אמר קרא ואם לא יגאל את השדה וגו' והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל - ורבי אליעזר מפרש ליה ודריש ליה הכי ואם לא יגאל לא יגאל עוד ואם מכר גזבר את השדה והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל לכהנים הא שמע מינה דאם לא מכר גזבר את השדה לא נפיק לכהנים:
notes.en: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer? Rabba said: The verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field,” etc., “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee”: Rabbi Eliezer explains it and interprets it thus: “And if he will not redeem,” “it shall not be redeemed anymore”; “and if” the [Temple] treasurer “sold the field,” “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” [shall be] for the priests. Conclude from this that if the treasurer did not sell the field, it does not go out to the priests.

messages.text: Does a sharp knife cut through the verses, that they may be interpreted by reading the words out of order?

notes.he: הא לא כתיבי הכי אלא הכי כתיבי לא יגאל עוד והיה השדה בצאתו לכהנים דמשמע דמשהגיע יובל לא תגאל עוד ותיפוק לכהנים אפי' לא מכרה גזבר:
notes.en: Does a sharp knife cut the verses?: They are not written that way; rather, they are written thus: “It shall not be redeemed anymore. But the field, when it goes out … for the priest,” which implies that once the Jubilee has arrived it may not be redeemed anymore, and it goes out to the priests even if the treasurer did not sell it.

notes.dh: אמר אביי סכינא חריפא מפסקא קראי
notes.he: כלומר דהאי לא יגאל משוי ליה נמי אלפני פניו [אאם לא יגאל והאי והיה השדה משוי ליה נמי אלפני פניו] אואם מכר וכי מי חתכם והפסיקם:
notes.en: Abaye said: Does a sharp knife cut the verses?: That is, this one attaches “it shall not be redeemed” to what is before it, to “and if he will not redeem,” and attaches “But the field” to what is before it, to “and if he sold.” Who cut them and separated them?

messages.text: The reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion is as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: וא"ת והלא פשטיה דקרא כרבי אליעזר משתמע ואם לא יגאל השדה הבעלים ואם מכר כלומר אלא שמכרו הגזבר לאיש אחר והיה בצאתו ביובל לכהנים אלמא אינו יוצא לכהנים כ"א בנמכר לאחר אבל לא גאלו אחר ועדיין ביד הגזבר אז אינו יוצא לכהנים אלמא פשטיה דקרא כרבי אליעזר משתמע ולפי מה שפירשתי דואם לא יגאל ואם מכר שני דרכים הם בזה ניחא דמשמע דבשני אלו יוצא לכהנים:
notes.en: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer: And if you say: but the plain sense of the verse is understood as Rabbi Eliezer holds: “And if he will not redeem the field,” the owner; “and if he sold,” that is, rather the treasurer sold it to another man; “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee” [shall be] for the priests. Evidently it goes out to the priests only when it was sold to another; but if another did not redeem it and it is still in the hand of the treasurer, then it does not go out to the priests. Evidently the plain sense of the verse is understood as Rabbi Eliezer holds [so why ask his reason]? But according to what I explained, that “and if he will not redeem” and “and if he sold” are two paths, this is fine, for it implies that in both of these it goes out to the priests.

messages.text: Since the verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed,” one might have thought that this means it shall not be redeemed at all by its owner, even for it to be treated for him like a purchased field, which remains in his possession until the Jubilee.

verse.he: וְאִם־לֹא יִגְאַל אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה וְאִם־מָכַר אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶה לְאִישׁ אַחֵר לֹא יִגָּאֵל עוֹד׃
verse.en: But if the one [who consecrated it] did not redeem the land, and the land was sold to another party, it shall no longer be redeemable:

notes.he: לבעלים אפי' להיות לפניו כשדה מקנה כשאר איש אחר הגואלה מיד הקדש שיוצאה מידו לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: One might have thought it may not be redeemed: by the owner, even for it to be before him like a purchased field, like any other person who redeems it from the Temple treasury, from whose possession it goes out to the priests at the Jubilee.

notes.dh: אלא אמר אביי טעמא דרבי אלעזר כדתניא לא יגאל יכול לא תהא נגאלת
notes.he: לאחר היובל שתהא לפניו לגואלה אפי' [בתורת] שדה מקנה שתהא שלו עד היובל וביובל תחזור להקדש:
notes.en: Rather, Abaye said: The reason of Rabbi Elazar is as it is taught: “It shall not be redeemed”; one might have thought it may not be redeemed after the Jubilee so as to be before him to redeem, even as a purchased field, so that it is his until the Jubilee and returns to the Temple treasury at the Jubilee.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “Anymore,” indicating that it shall not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was, i.e., to regain the status of an ancestral field, but it may be redeemed for it to be treated for him like a purchased field.

notes.he: להיות שדה אחוזה שלא תצא מידו ביובל אינה נגאלת לו:
notes.en: As it was: to be an ancestral field, so that it would not go out of his possession at the Jubilee; [in that way] it is not redeemed for him.

messages.text: According to this baraita, of when, i.e., about which time period, is the verse speaking? If we say that it is referring to a redemption occurring during the first Jubilee cycle in which the field was consecrated, then why may it not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was? At that point, it is even redeemable as an ancestral field, because if the owner redeems it then, it is not removed from his possession during the Jubilee Year.

notes.dh: אילימא ביובל ראשון אמאי אינה נגאלת שדה אחוזה נמי הויא
notes.he: תימה הוה ליה למימר אילימא ביובל ראשון הכתיב ואם גאל יגאל את השדה וקם לו ושמא היינו הא דקאמר וא"ת הא יש לאוקמא ביובל ראשון כגון שגאלה אחר מיד הגזבר וגאלה ממנו הבעלים דאז הדין בו שהוא כשדה מקנה וחוזרת לכהנים ביובל כדתנן (לעיל ערכין דף כה.) גאלה אחר או אחד מן הקרובים וגאלה הוא יוצא מתחת ידו ביובל וי"ל דאין סברא דמיירי קרא (בהני) בגאולה הבאה מיד אחר ליד הבעלים דלא מיירי קרא אלא בגאולה מיד גזבר שהרי אם גאלה אחר לא ימכרנה לבעלים אם ירצה (ומיהו) [ומש"ה] לא מיירי לא יגאל עוד כי אם בגאולה הבאה מיד הגזבר:
notes.en: If we say in the first Jubilee, why may it not be redeemed? It is also an ancestral field: This is puzzling: he should have said: If we say in the first Jubilee, but it is written: “And if he will indeed redeem the field … it shall be established for him” [Leviticus 27:19]! And perhaps that is what he means. And if you say: one can establish it in the first Jubilee, for example where another redeemed it from the treasurer and the owner redeemed it from him, for then the law is that it is like a purchased field and returns to the priests at the Jubilee, as we learned (above, Arakhin 25a): If another redeemed it, or one of the relatives, and he redeemed it from him, it goes out from under his hand at the Jubilee. One can say: it is not reasonable that the verse speaks of a redemption that comes from the hand of another to the hand of the owner, for the verse speaks only of redemption from the hand of the treasurer, since if another redeemed it, he will not sell it to the owner unless he wishes. And therefore “it shall not be redeemed anymore” speaks only of a redemption that comes from the hand of the treasurer.

notes.he: ת"ל עוד כלומר מאחר שיצאה ביובל עוד לא תהא נגאלת שתהא דינה עוד כמו שהיתה כשדה אחוזה שתחזור לבעליה (שוב) ביובל אבל נגאלת לו בתורת שדה מקנה שתהא שלו עד שנת היובל וביובל תחזור להקדש משום דכיון דהגיע יובל ולא נגאלה קנאה הקדש כי חוזר זה וגאלה מהקדש הוי כלוקח. וכתיב והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל לכהן תהיה אחוזתו בשנת היובל ישוב השדה לאשר קנהו מאתו והיינו הקדש. וקא דייק אימת קאי [דקאמר] אבל נגאלת שתהא לפניו כשדה מקנה אילימא ביובל ראשון דאכתי לא הגיעה שנת היובל אמאי קאמר (עוד) לכמות שהיתה אינה נגאלת אמאי הא דין שדה אחוזה נמי אית לה הואיל ולא עבר היובל עדיין:
notes.en: The verse states “anymore”: that is, after it went out at the Jubilee, it may no longer be redeemed so that its law is again as it was, like an ancestral field that returns to its owner at the Jubilee; but it is redeemable for him as a purchased field, so that it is his until the Jubilee Year, and at the Jubilee it returns to the Temple treasury. For once the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed, the Temple treasury acquired it; when this one goes back and redeems it from the Temple treasury, he is like a buyer. And it is written: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee … his ancestral possession shall be for the priest”; “In the Jubilee Year the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought,” and that is the Temple treasury. And he infers: when does it apply, [that it says] “but it is redeemable to be before him like a purchased field”? If we say in the first Jubilee, when the Jubilee Year has not yet arrived, why does it say that it is not redeemable as it was? Why not? It still has the law of an ancestral field, since the Jubilee has not yet passed.

messages.text: Rather, it is obvious that the baraita interprets the verse as referring to a redemption occurring during the second Jubilee cycle.

notes.he: קאי תנא דברייתא [ולמאן קתני ברייתא] אבל נגאלת שתהא לפניו כשדה מקנה כלומר דקא הדרא להקדש:
notes.en: Rather, it is obvious [that it refers to] the second Jubilee: [that is where] the tanna of the baraita stands, [and according to whom does he teach the baraita:] “but it is redeemable to be before him like a purchased field,” that is, it returns to the Temple treasury.

messages.text: And according to whose opinion is this baraita? If we say that it is according to either Rabbi Yehuda or Rabbi Shimon, this cannot be correct, as according to them, the field leaves the possession of the Temple treasury and is given to the priests during the first Jubilee Year, after which it may no longer be redeemed.

notes.he: לרבי יהודה בדמים ולר"ש בחנם וסוף סוף בעליה לא יגאלנה שוב לגמרי:
notes.en: It goes out to the priests: according to Rabbi Yehuda for money, and according to Rabbi Shimon for free; and in the end its owner can no longer redeem it at all.

notes.dh: אי לר' יהודה ור' שמעון לכהנים הוא דנפקא
notes.he: אפי' מיובל ראשון כדתנן הכהנים נכנסין לתוכה למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה ומאחר דנפקא לכהנים שוב אינה נגאלת מידם בתורת חומר שעורים בנ' שקל כסף אלא בשוויה בין בפרדסות סבסטי בין בחולת המחוז:
notes.en: If according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, it goes out to the priests: even from the first Jubilee, as we learned: The priests enter into it, one Sage as he holds and the other Sage as he holds. And once it has gone out to the priests, it is no longer redeemable from them by the measure of a ḥomer of barley for fifty shekels of silver, but [only] at its value, whether among the orchards of Sebaste or in the sandy soil of the district.

messages.text: Rather, is it not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who maintains that the field remains in the possession of the Temple treasury until it is redeemed, even during a subsequent Jubilee cycle?

notes.he: דאמר שני נמי בת גאולה היא אי לאו איפרקא ביובל ראשון:
notes.en: Is it not Rabbi Eliezer: who says that in the second [Jubilee cycle] too it is redeemable, if it was not redeemed in the first Jubilee.

notes.he: מדקתני נגאלת (דהיינו) דמשמע בנ' שקל ש"מ (אמר) לר' אלעזר קאמר דסבירא ליה דשל הקדש היה ביובל הראשון:
notes.en: Rather, is it not: since it teaches “redeemable,” which implies for fifty shekels, conclude from this that it is stated according to Rabbi Elazar, who holds that it belonged to the Temple treasury at the first Jubilee.

messages.text: And consequently, conclude from this baraita that the reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion is from here, i.e., from the superfluous term “anymore.”

notes.he: מדאיצטריך האי עוד לאשמועינן דנגאלת היא לו להיות לפניו כשדה מקנה ולא מיתוקם האי קרא אלא ביובל שני ש"מ ביובל שני עומדת היא ליגאל:
notes.en: And the reason of Rabbi Eliezer is from here: since this “anymore” was needed to teach us that it is redeemable for him, to be before him like a purchased field, and this verse can be established only in the second Jubilee, conclude from this that in the second Jubilee it still stands to be redeemed.

messages.text: And can you understand the baraita this way? If so, then what do Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon derive from this term: “Anymore”?
messages.quote: the reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion is from here

notes.he: ותיסברא דהא כדקא מתרת בשלמא לר' אלעזר דאמר דשל הקדש הוא [ניחא] האי עוד כדקאמרת עוד אינה נגאלת כלומר דבת גאולה היא בנ' שקל דאכתי דהקדש היא:
notes.en: And can you understand it as you have resolved it?: Granted, according to Rabbi Elazar, who says it belongs to the Temple treasury, this “anymore” is [fine] as you said: “it shall not be redeemed anymore,” that is, it is redeemable for fifty shekels, as it still belongs to the Temple treasury.

notes.dh: אלא לר' יהודה ור' שמעון דאמרי
notes.he: דשל כהנים היא האי עוד מאי דרשי ביה הא לאו בת גאולה היא כלל בנ' שקל אלא בשוויה אי הכי מאי קמ"ל האי עוד:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, who say: it belongs to the priests, what do they interpret from this “anymore”? It is not redeemable at all for fifty shekels, only at its value; if so, what does this “anymore” teach us?

messages.text: Rather, the baraita can be understood in accordance with their opinions as well, and what are we dealing with here? We are dealing with an ancestral field whose owner consecrated it and did not redeem it, which left the possession of the Temple treasury and was given to the priests during the first Jubilee Year; and the priest who received the field then consecrated it, and then the original owner came to redeem it from the Temple treasury.

notes.he: שהקדיש אדם שדה אחוזה וגאלה אחר ויצאתה מידו לכהנים והקדישה ביובל שני ואתו בעלים למיפרקה מיד גזבר:
notes.en: Which went out to the priests: where a person consecrated an ancestral field and another redeemed it, and it went out of his possession to the priests; and [the priest] consecrated it in the second Jubilee [cycle], and the owner came to redeem it from the treasurer. [Rashi describes the field as redeemed by another before it went to the priests; the Davidson English says only that the owner did not redeem it.]

notes.he: ברייתא בשדה שיצאה לכהנים כדסברי [ר"י ור"ש] ונפקא לכהנים ואח"כ הקדישה כהן [או כהן] אחד חלקו או הקדישו כולה בית אב דכיון דבאת ליד הקדש בת גאולה היא בנ' שקל כסף ואתו בעלים למיפרקא סד"א כיון דנפקא לה [כבר] לכהנים לא תיפוק תו ליד בעלים אפי' בתורת שדה מקנה ת"ל עוד לכמות שהיתה בתורת שדה אחוזה אינה נגאלת שתהא לבעלים אבל נגאלת שתהא לפניו כשדה מקנה וחוזרת [לכהנים] (לבעלים) ביובל ואכתי לא שמעינן טעמא דר' אלעזר:
notes.en: Rather, what are we dealing with here: The baraita [speaks] of a field that went out to the priests, as [Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon] hold, and it went out to the priests; and afterward a priest consecrated it, [or] one priest [consecrated] his share, or the [priestly] family consecrated all of it. Since it came into the hand of the Temple treasury, it is redeemable for fifty shekels of silver, and the owner came to redeem it. It might enter your mind to say: since it has [already] gone out to the priests, it shall no longer go out to the hand of the owner, even as a purchased field. The verse states “anymore”: as it was, as an ancestral field, it is not redeemable to belong to the owner, but it is redeemable to be before him like a purchased field, and it returns [to the priests] at the Jubilee. And we have still not heard the reason of Rabbi Elazar.

messages.text: It might enter your mind to say: Since the owner failed to redeem this field during the first Jubilee cycle, it shall not be redeemed by him at all, even for it to be treated for him like a purchased field. Therefore, the verse states: “Anymore,” indicating that it shall not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was, i.e., an ancestral field, but it may be redeemed for it to be treated for him like a purchased field, which remains in his possession only until the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: כלל הואיל ולא גאלה בהקדש ראשון כשהקדישה הוא:
notes.en: It might enter your mind to say it may not be redeemed: at all, since he did not redeem it from the first consecration, when he himself consecrated it.

notes.he: שתהא לפניו כשדה מקנה וכשיגיע יובל תצא מידו ותתחלק לכהנים:
notes.en: The verse states “anymore”: that it shall be before him like a purchased field, and when the Jubilee arrives it goes out of his possession and is divided among the priests.

messages.text: And similarly, it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: בניחותא דדרשי' הכי:
notes.en: And similarly it is taught: [read it] as a plain statement, for we interpret [the verse] this way.

messages.text: With regard to one who consecrated a purchased field and redeemed it, since the verse states: “In the Jubilee Year the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought” (Leviticus 27:24), one might have thought that the field shall return to the Temple treasurer, from whom he bought it when he redeemed it. Therefore, the verse states immediately afterward: “To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs,” i.e., it goes to the ancestral owner who initially sold the field to the one who consecrated it.

verse.he: בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל יָשׁוּב הַשָּׂדֶה לַאֲשֶׁר קָנָהוּ מֵאִתּוֹ לַאֲשֶׁר־לוֹ אֲחֻזַּת הָאָרֶץ׃
verse.en: In the jubilee year the land shall revert to the one from whom it was bought, whose holding the land is.

notes.he: במקדיש שדה מקנה כתיב וגאלה לזה:
notes.en: In the Jubilee Year the field shall return: this is written about one who consecrates a purchased field, and this one redeemed it.

notes.he: דהיינו בעלים ראשונים שמכרה לאותו שהקדישה:
notes.en: The verse states: “To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs”: that is, the original owner, who sold it to the one who consecrated it.

notes.he: האי בשדה מקנה כתיב לאשר קנהו מאתו יכול אפי' לגזבר שלקחו ממנו שאם היה לו שדה מקנה והקדישה וחזר ולקחה מן הגזבר וכשהגיע היובל יכול שתשוב השדה לגזבר שלקחה ממנו דקרינן ביה לאשר קנהו מאתו ת"ל לאשר לו אחוזת הארץ:
notes.en: In the Jubilee Year the field shall return: this is written about a purchased field. “To the one from whom it was bought”: one might have thought even to the treasurer from whom he bought it; that is, if he had a purchased field and consecrated it, and then bought it back from the treasurer, when the Jubilee arrives one might have thought the field returns to the treasurer from whom he bought it, since we can read of it “to the one from whom it was bought.” The verse states: “To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs.”

notes.he: [למוכר ראשון חוזרת דאין אדם מקדיש דבר שאינו שלו ולא לגזבר:
notes.en: It returns to the first seller, for a person cannot consecrate an item that is not his, and not to the treasurer. [The printed text marks this note and the opening of the next as an added passage.]

messages.text: If so, let the verse simply state: “To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs.” Why must the verse state first: “To the one from whom it was bought”?

notes.he: ולא היה צריך לאשר קנהו [מה ת"ל לאשר קנהו] אלא לשדה שיצאת לכהנים ומכרה כהן והקדישה לוקח וגאלה אחר יכול כיון שגאלה אחר ולא גאלה לוקח והרי היא יוצאה מיד זה שגאלה וחוזרת ביובל הואיל ויש כאן חזרה כל כך שבאת ליד שלישי יכול תחזור לבעלים הראשונים ת"ל לאשר קנהו כלומר ליד הכהן שמכרה חוזרת ולא לבעלים והיינו סיועא דחוזרת לכהנים:
notes.en: Let it state “to the one to whom the possession of the land belongs,” and it would not need “to the one from whom it was bought”; why does the verse state “to the one from whom it was bought”? Rather, [it is needed] for a field that went out to the priests, and a priest sold it, and the buyer consecrated it, and another redeemed it. One might have thought: since another redeemed it and the buyer did not redeem it, and it goes out of the hand of this one who redeemed it and returns at the Jubilee, since there is so much returning here, that it came into the hand of a third person, one might have thought it returns to the original owners. The verse states “to the one from whom it was bought,” that is, it returns to the hand of the priest who sold it, and not to the owners. And this is a support [for the view] that it returns to the priests.

messages.text: The verse is referring to an ancestral field whose owner consecrated it and did not redeem it, which left the possession of the Temple treasury and was given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, and the priest who received the field then sold it to another, and the buyer then consecrated it, and another person redeemed it from the Temple treasury. One might have thought that when the next Jubilee arrives, it shall return to the original owner. Therefore, the verse states: “In the Jubilee Year the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought,” indicating that the field is returned to the priest who sold the field.

notes.he: לאותו שהקדישה הקדש ראשון שהרי לו אחוזת הארץ:
notes.en: One might have thought it returns to the original owner: to the one who consecrated it in the first consecration, since “the possession of the land” is his.

notes.he: והרי לא נקנית מאתו אלא ע"י הקדש יצתה מידו אלא לכהן חוזרת שממנו קנאה לוקח זה שהקדישה והיינו נמי דלעיל דמאחר שהקדישה ראשון שהיתה לו אחוזה וגאלה אחר ויצתה לכהנים תו לא הדרא ליה אי לא פריק ליה:
notes.en: The verse states “to the one from whom it was bought”: and it was not bought from him; rather, it left his possession through consecration. Rather, it returns to the priest, from whom this buyer who consecrated it bought it. And this is also [the case] above: once the first one, for whom it was an ancestral field, consecrated it, and another redeemed it and it went out to the priests, it no longer returns to him unless he redeems it.

messages.text: And it was necessary for the Torah to write: “It shall not be redeemed,” and it was also necessary for it to write: “To the one from whom it was bought,” despite the fact both phrases apparently teach the same halakha, i.e., that after a consecrated ancestral field is left unredeemed and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, it never returns to the original owner.

notes.he: לאשמועינן כדאמרן דהיכא דהקדיש שדה אחוזה ולא גאלה וגאלה אחר ויצתה לכהנים ומכרה כהן ביובל שני והקדישה לוקח וגאלה אחר דלא הדרא ביובל למרה קמא שהקדישה תחילה:
notes.en: And it was necessary to write “to the one from whom it was bought”: to teach us, as we said, that where one consecrated an ancestral field and did not redeem it, and another redeemed it and it went out to the priests, and a priest sold it in the second Jubilee [cycle], and the buyer consecrated it and another redeemed it, it does not return at the Jubilee to the first owner, who consecrated it originally.

notes.he: דאוקימנא לעיל נמי בהכי דהקדישה וגאלה אחר ויצתה לכהנים והקדישה כהן תו לא מצי פריק לה ראשון להיות לפניו כשדה אחוזה הואיל דיצתה מהקדש ראשון לכהנים:
notes.en: And it was necessary to write “it shall not be redeemed”: as we also established it above in this way: he consecrated it and another redeemed it and it went out to the priests, and a priest consecrated it; the first one can no longer redeem it to be before him like an ancestral field, since it went out from the first consecration to the priests.

messages.text: Because if the Merciful One had written only: “It shall not be redeemed,” one might have thought that the field does not return to the original owner only in a case where the priest consecrates the field and the original owner redeems it, as an ancestral field that is consecrated by its owner and redeemed by another does not return at all, but is divided among the priests.

notes.he: היכא דהקדישה כהן לא הדרא לשום אדם לעולם שהרי שדה אחוזה הואי לגבי כהן דכתיב לכהן תהיה אחוזתו וכי מקדיש לה כהן דין שדה אחוזה אית לה ולכשיגאלנה אחר מיד הקדש תצא ביובל ותתחלק לכל הכהנים אבל לכהן המקדישה לא תחזור אלא כחלק שאר אחיו והלכך נמי לא הדרא לבעלים קמאי להיות לפניו כשדה אחוזה:
notes.en: As it does not return at all: where a priest consecrated it, it never returns to anyone, since it was an ancestral field with respect to the priest, as it is written: “His ancestral possession shall be for the priest.” And when a priest consecrates it, it has the law of an ancestral field, and once another redeems it from the Temple treasury it goes out at the Jubilee and is divided among all the priests; to the priest who consecrated it, it returns only as a share like the rest of his brethren. And therefore it also does not return to the first owners to be before him like an ancestral field.

messages.text: But here, where the priest sold the field that he received and the field was consecrated by the buyer as a purchased field and subsequently redeemed by another, as the field does return to its owner in the Jubilee Year, perhaps it should return to its original owner, and not the priest. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote: “To the one from whom it was bought,” indicating that it returns to the priest.

notes.he: מכר כהן והקדישה לוקח דהשתא שדה מקנה הוא וכי פריק לה איניש מיד הקדש ומטי יובל לא נפקא לכהנים אלא הדרא אימא תיהדר למרה קמא שהקדישה תחלה שהרי לו אחוזת הארץ קמ"ל לאשר קנהו מאתו דהיינו לכהן שלקחה מקדיש האחרון ממנו:
notes.en: But: where a priest sold it and the buyer consecrated it, it is now a purchased field; and when a person redeems it from the Temple treasury and the Jubilee arrives, it does not go out to the priests but returns. I would say it should return to its first owner, who consecrated it originally, since “the possession of the land” is his. [The verse] teaches us “to the one from whom it was bought,” that is, to the priest, from whom the last one who consecrated it bought it.

notes.he: ולאשר קנהו מאתו למילף מתרוייהו דלכהנים הדרא ולא לבעלים דאי מלא יגאל לחודיה הוה אמינא מ"ט לא הדרא לבעלים ביובל דכתיב ביה לא יגאל דלא קא הדרא כלל שכן יצאת מרשות בעלים וחוזרת לכהנים ואין כאן חוזרת כל כך ועוד דלא כתיב בההוא קרא ישוב אבל הכא דקא הדרא דכתיב ביה ישוב השדה ועוד שיש כאן חוזרת הרבה שבאת ליד שלישי הואיל והדרא דכתיב ישוב אימא תיהדר לבעלים להכי כתיב לאשר קנהו לכהן שמכרה:
notes.en: And it was necessary to write “it shall not be redeemed” and “to the one from whom it was bought,” to learn from both of them that it returns to the priests and not to the owners. For if [it had written] only “it shall not be redeemed,” I would have said: what is the reason it does not return to the owners at the Jubilee? Because “it shall not be redeemed” is written of it, for it does not return at all, since it left the owners’ domain and returns to the priests, and there is not so much returning here; and furthermore, “shall return” is not written in that verse. But here, where it does return, as “the field shall return” is written of it, and furthermore there is much returning here, since it came into the hand of a third person: since it returns, as it is written “shall return,” I would say it should return to the owners. Therefore it is written “to the one from whom it was bought,” to the priest who sold it.

messages.text: And if the Merciful One had written only: “To the one from whom it was bought,” one might have thought that the field does not return to its original owner during the Jubilee Year only in a case where the priest sold it and the buyer consecrated it, as the owner did not give any payment for the field to the Temple treasury. But here, where the priest consecrated the field and its original owner redeemed it, as he gives payment for the field to the Temple treasury, perhaps it should remain in his hands as his ancestral field. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote: “It shall not be redeemed.”

notes.he: לעולם כשדה אחוזה ולא תיפוק ביובל לכהנים כשדה מקנה כשאר אדם הקונה שדה אחוזה מיד הקדש דהויא שדה מקנה לגביה ונפקא מיניה לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: It should remain in his hands: forever, like an ancestral field, and not go out to the priests at the Jubilee like a purchased field, like any other person who acquires an ancestral field from the Temple treasury, for whom it is a purchased field and from whom it goes out to the priests at the Jubilee.

notes.he: ואי כתיב לאשר קנהו לחודיה וכדתרצינן דמכרה כהן והקדישה לוקח וגאלה אחר משום הכי לא הדרא לבעלים דלא קא יהבו בעלים דמי לגזבר אלא גאלה אחר אבל הכא בהאי לא יגאל עוד דאמרן לעיל דהקדישה כהן ואתו בעלים למיפרקיה דקא יהבי בעלים [דמי] אימא תיקום ברשותייהו:
notes.en: And if it had written only “to the one from whom it was bought,” as we explained, where a priest sold it and the buyer consecrated it and another redeemed it, [I would say] that is why it does not return to the owners: because the owners did not give money to the treasurer; rather, another redeemed it. But here, in this “it shall not be redeemed anymore” that we discussed above, where a priest consecrated it and the owners came to redeem it, since the owners give [money], I would say it should remain in their domain.

notes.he: דלא תהדר לבעלים:
notes.en: The Merciful One wrote “it shall not be redeemed”: that it does not return to the owners.

messages.text: And if the Merciful One had written only: “It shall not be redeemed,” and did not write: “Anymore,” I would say that it shall not be redeemed at all, as its original owner failed to redeem it during the first Jubilee cycle. Therefore, the Merciful One writes: “Anymore,” to indicate that it shall not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was, i.e., an ancestral field, but it may be redeemed for it to be treated for him like a purchased field.

messages.caption: The two cases the Gemara reads into the verses once a field has gone out to the priests, and why each verse is needed.

messages.text: What conclusion was reached about it? In other words, now that both suggestions have been rejected, what is the reason for Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion that a consecrated ancestral field that has not been redeemed by the Jubilee Year is not given to the priests?
messages.quote: The priests do not enter into the field

notes.he: טעמא דרבי אליעזר מהיכא:
notes.en: What was concluded about it: from where is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?

notes.he: דאכתי לא ידעינן טעמא דר' אלעזר דאמר לעיל אין הכהנים נכנסים עד שיגאלנה אחר:
notes.en: What was concluded about it: for we still do not know the reason of Rabbi Elazar, who said above: The priests do not enter until another redeems it.

messages.text: The verse states: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be holy for the Lord, as a dedicated field; his ancestral possession shall be for the priest” (Leviticus 27:21). The term “when it goes out” indicates that it is given to the priests only when it goes out during the Jubilee Year from the possession of another person, who redeemed it from the Temple treasury.

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: משמע כשתצא מיד הגואל אותה כדין שדה אדם הקונה קרקע שיוצאה ביובל בההוא קאמר דתיהוי לכהנים אבל ביציאתו מיד הקדש לא משמע דאכתי לא אשמעינן קרא הקדש יהא יוצא ביובל (מכח בדק הבית):
notes.en: When it goes out: implies when it goes out of the hand of the one who redeemed it, according to the law of a person who buys land, which goes out at the Jubilee; with regard to that it says that it shall be for the priests. But its going out from the hand of the Temple treasury is not implied, for the verse has not yet taught us that consecrated property goes out at the Jubilee (by force of Temple maintenance).

notes.dh: אמר רבא דאמר קרא והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל
notes.he: דהוה יכול למימר והיה השדה ביובל קודש לה' וגו' מאי בצאתו קא משמע לן דכשיוצא מיד אחר שגאלה מיד הגזבר (אחר) [קודם] היובל [או] לקחה מגזבר אח"כ לכהן תהיה אחוזתו:
notes.en: Rava said: Because the verse states: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee”: for it could have said: “But the field in the Jubilee shall be holy for the Lord,” etc. What is [taught by] “when it goes out”? It teaches us that when it goes out of the hand of another, who redeemed it from the hand of the treasurer [before] the Jubilee [or] bought it from the treasurer, then “his ancestral possession shall be for the priest.”

messages.text: According to Rabbi Eliezer, if the owner consecrated his ancestral field and failed to redeem it before the first Jubilee Year, but he redeemed it during the second Jubilee cycle, is he considered like another person who redeemed the field, in which case it is given to the priests at the following Jubilee Year, or not, i.e., as the one who ultimately redeemed the field first was the owner, does it remain in his possession as it would have if he had redeemed it during the first Jubilee cycle?
messages.lead: § A dilemma was raised before the Sages:

notes.he: לרבי אליעזר דאמר ביובל שני בת גאולה היא אם לא נגאלה בראשון:
notes.en: A dilemma was raised before them: according to Rabbi Eliezer, who says that in the second Jubilee [cycle] it is redeemable if it was not redeemed in the first.

notes.he: ואי פריק לה יוצאה מידו לכהנים:
notes.en: Is the owner in the second Jubilee like another: so that if he redeems it, it goes out of his possession to the priests?

notes.he: כאחר דמו אלא כי היכי דאילו פרקה ביובל ראשון הוה קיימא בידיה השתא נמי קיימא בידיה:
notes.en: Or not: are they not like another; rather, just as, had he redeemed it in the first Jubilee [cycle], it would remain in his possession, now too it remains in his possession?

notes.he: פירוש לרבי אליעזר כאחר דמו או לא דכיון דלא גאלה ולא נתחלקה לכהנים ביובל שעדיין היא ביד הגזבר יכולים הבעלים לגאלה דהא דכתיב לא יגאל עוד כדדרשינן מיניה שאינה נגאלת לכמו שהיתה היינו שגאלה אחר מיד הגזבר ובלא נתחלקה מעולם לכהנים בהכי לא מיירי ביה קרא דלא יגאל עוד אלא תעמוד ביד הבעלים כשגאלה מיד הגזבר:
notes.en: A dilemma was raised before them: Is the owner in the second Jubilee [like another]? Explanation: according to Rabbi Eliezer, are they like another or not? For since it was not redeemed and was not divided among the priests at the Jubilee, as it is still in the hand of the treasurer, the owners can redeem it. For what is written, “it shall not be redeemed anymore,” which we interpret to mean that it is not redeemed [to be] as it was, refers to where another redeemed it from the treasurer; but where it was never divided among the priests, the verse “it shall not be redeemed anymore” does not speak of that, and it should remain in the hand of the owners when they redeem it from the treasurer.

notes.he: לרבי אלעזר בעלים כאחר דמו ויוצאה שוב לכהנים או לא דמו לגאלה אחר:
notes.en: The owners redeemed it in the second Jubilee: according to Rabbi Elazar, are the owners like another, so that it again goes out to the priests, or are they not like [a case where] another redeemed it?

messages.text: Come and hear a resolution of this dilemma from the following baraita:

Since the verse states: “And if he will not redeem the field, or if he sold the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed” (Leviticus 27:20), one might have thought that this means it shall not be redeemed at all by its owner, even for it to be treated for him like a purchased field. Therefore, the verse states: “Anymore,” indicating that it shall not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was, i.e., an ancestral field, but it may be redeemed for it to be treated for him like a purchased field.

According to this baraita, of when, i.e., about which time period, is the verse speaking? If we say that it is referring to a redemption that occurs during the first Jubilee cycle, in which the field was consecrated, why may it not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was? At that point it is even redeemable as an ancestral field, since if the owner redeems it then, it is not removed from his possession during the Jubilee Year. Rather, it is obvious that the baraita interprets the verse as referring to a redemption occurring during the second Jubilee cycle.

And according to whose opinion is this baraita? If we say that it is according to either Rabbi Yehuda or Rabbi Shimon, this cannot be correct, as according to them, the field leaves the possession of the Temple treasury and is given to the priests during the first Jubilee Year, after which it may no longer be redeemed.

notes.he: וביובל שני לאו בת גאולה היא כלל:
notes.en: It goes out to the priests: and in the second Jubilee [cycle] it is not redeemable at all.

messages.text: Rather, is it not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer, who maintains that the field remains in the possession of the Temple treasury until it is redeemed, even during a subsequent Jubilee cycle? And consequently, you can conclude from this baraita that according to Rabbi Eliezer, an owner who redeems his ancestral field from the Temple treasury during the second Jubilee cycle is considered like another, as he may redeem it only for it to be treated like a purchased field.

notes.dh: ת"ש לא יגאל עוד כו' אלא פשיטא ביובל שני
notes.he: ונגאלת שתהיה לפניו כשדה מקנה שחוזרת לכהנים ביובל כדכתיב לכהן תהיה וגו' אלמא דבעלים ביובל שני כאחר דמו:
notes.en: Come and hear: “It shall not be redeemed anymore,” etc. Rather, it is obvious [that it refers to] the second Jubilee, and it is redeemable to be before him like a purchased field, which returns to the priests at the Jubilee, as it is written: “Shall be for the priest,” etc. Evidently the owners in the second Jubilee are like another.

messages.text: And can you understand the baraita this way? If so, what do Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon derive from this term: “Anymore”?
messages.quote: an owner who redeems his ancestral field from the Temple treasury during the second Jubilee cycle is considered like another

notes.he: ומדחי ליה דליכא למשמע טעמא מהכא:
notes.en: And can you understand it, etc.: and he rejects it, [saying] that the reason cannot be learned from here.

messages.text: Rather, what are we dealing with here? We are dealing with an ancestral field whose owner consecrated it and did not redeem it, which left the possession of the Temple treasury and was given to the priests at the first Jubilee Year; and the priest who received the field subsequently consecrated it, and then the original owner came to redeem it from the Temple treasury.

notes.dh: אלא הכא במאי עסקינן בשדה שיצתה לכהנים
notes.he: פירוש כגון שדה אחוזה שהקדישה בעלים וגאלה אחר לפני היובל שיוצאה לכהנים ביובל ובא כהן אשר הגיע לו אותו שדה והקדיש והיינו ביובל שני ואתו בעלים למיפרק דסד"א אי לא כתיב (כי) אם לא יגאל דלא תפריק שתהא לפניו אפי' כשדה מקנה ת"ל עוד לכמות שהיתה אינה נגאלת [אבל נגאלת] שתהא כשדה מקנה פירוש ותחזור לכהנים ביובל והשתא קאי והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל וגו' אשני דרכים דמיירי בהו קרא בין אואם לא יגאל השדה בין אואם מכר לאיש אחר דלעולם קרא בשני ענינים איירי כדפירשתי לעיל וא"כ לר"א נמי פירושא דקרא הכי הוא ולעיל מיבעי לי' מאי טעם דרבי אליעזר ומסיק מאי הוי עלה (פירוש מ"ט) דרבי אליעזר אמר רבא אמר קרא והיה השדה בצאתו ביובל וגו' בצאתו מתחת ידי אחר פירוש כי ביציאתו משמע שיוצא מיד אחר שגאלה מיד הגזבר אבל כל זמן שהיא ביד הגזבר לא יצא ביובל:
notes.en: Rather, what are we dealing with here? With a field that went out to the priests: Explanation: for example, an ancestral field that its owners consecrated and another redeemed before the Jubilee, which goes out to the priests at the Jubilee; and the priest to whom that field fell came and consecrated it, and this is in the second Jubilee [cycle], and the owners came to redeem it. For it might enter your mind, if only “it shall not be redeemed” were written, that he may not redeem it to be before him even like a purchased field. The verse states “anymore”: as it was, it is not redeemed, [but it is redeemed] to be like a purchased field, meaning that it returns to the priests at the Jubilee. And now “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee,” etc., refers to the two paths the verse speaks of, both “and if he will not redeem the field” and “and if he sold the field to another man,” for the verse in fact speaks of two matters, as I explained above. And if so, according to Rabbi Eliezer too this is the explanation of the verse; and above he asks: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer? And he concludes: What was concluded about it, (that is, what is the reason) of Rabbi Eliezer? Rava said: The verse states: “But the field, when it goes out in the Jubilee,” etc., “when it goes out” from under the hand of another. Explanation: for “when it goes out” implies that it goes out of the hand of another who redeemed it from the hand of the treasurer; but as long as it is in the hand of the treasurer, it does not go out at the Jubilee.

messages.text: It may enter your mind to say: Since the owner failed to redeem it during the first Jubilee cycle, it shall not be redeemed by him at all, even for it to be treated for him like a purchased field. Therefore, the verse states: “Anymore,” indicating that it shall not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was, i.e., an ancestral field, but it may be redeemed for it to be treated for him like a purchased field.
And similarly, it is taught in a baraita:

With regard to one who consecrated a purchased field and redeemed it, since the verse states: “In the Jubilee Year the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought” (Leviticus 27:24), one might have thought that the field shall return to the Temple treasurer, from whom he bought it when he redeemed it. Therefore, the verse states: “To the one to whom the possession of the land belongs,” i.e., the ancestral owner.

If so, why must the verse state: “To the one from whom it was bought”? The verse is referring to an ancestral field that was consecrated and not redeemed, and which therefore left the possession of the Temple treasury and was given to the priests at the Jubilee Year, and the priest who received the field then sold it to another, and the buyer then consecrated it, and another person redeemed it from the Temple treasury. One might have thought that when the next Jubilee arrives, it shall return to the original owner. Therefore, the verse states: “In the Jubilee Year the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought,” indicating that the field is returned to the priest who sold the field.

And it was necessary for the Torah to write: “It shall not be redeemed,” and it was also necessary for it to write: “To the one from whom it was bought,” because if the Merciful One had written merely: “It shall not be redeemed,” one might have thought that the field does not return to the original owner only in a case where the priest consecrates the field and the original owner redeems it, as an ancestral field that is consecrated by its owner and redeemed by another does not return at all. But in a case where the priest sold the field to another and the buyer consecrated it, perhaps it should return to its original owner. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote: “To the one from whom it was bought,” indicating that it returns to the priest.

And if the Merciful One had written merely: “To the one from whom it was bought,” one might think that the field does not return to its original owner at the Jubilee Year only in a case where the priest sold it and the buyer consecrated it, as the owner did not give any payment for the field to the Temple treasury. But here, where the priest consecrated the field and its original owner redeemed it, as the owner gives payment for the field to the Temple treasury, one might have thought that it should remain in his hands, as his ancestral field. Therefore, the Merciful One wrote: “It shall not be redeemed.”

And if the Merciful One had written only: “It shall not be redeemed,” and did not write: “Anymore,” I would say that it shall not be redeemed at all, as its original owner failed to redeem it during the first Jubilee cycle. Therefore, the Merciful One writes: “Anymore,” to indicate that it shall not be redeemed in order for it to return to the way it was, but it may be redeemed for it to be treated for him like a purchased field.

Since it has been established that the term “anymore” is necessary according to all opinions, what conclusion was reached about the original dilemma with regard to whether the owner is considered like another person during the second Jubilee cycle? Come and hear a proof from the following baraita:
messages.quote: is he considered like another person who redeemed the field

notes.dh: מאי הוי עלה אמר רבא ת"ש
notes.he: דתנינן ברייתא בפירוש דכאחר דמו ר"א אומר כו':
notes.en: What was concluded about it? Rava said: Come and hear: for we learned a baraita explicitly that they are like another: Rabbi Eliezer says, etc. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text has “Rava said” here; the daf reads only “Come and hear.”]

messages.text: If the owner redeemed it during the second Jubilee cycle, it leaves the possession of the Temple treasury and is given to the priests during the Jubilee Year.

@Rav Ashi But we did not learn this interpretation of Rabbi Eliezer’s opinion in the mishna. Instead, the mishna states that Rabbi Eliezer says: The priests never enter into a consecrated field during the Jubilee Year until another person redeems it first. This indicates that if the owner, rather than any other person, is the one who ultimately redeems the field, it remains in his possession even if he did so during the second Jubilee cycle.
messages.quote: it leaves the possession of the Temple treasury and is given to the priests

messages.text: @Ravina During the second Jubilee cycle, the owner is considered like another person.
If the owner redeemed it during the second Jubilee cycle, it does not leave the possession of the Temple treasury and is not given to the priests during the Jubilee Year.
messages.lead: Some say a different version of the baraita and ensuing discussion:

messages.text: @Rav Ashi Why must a proof be brought from this baraita? We learn in the mishna as well that Rabbi Eliezer says: The priests never enter into a consecrated field during the Jubilee Year until another person redeems it first.

@Ravina If a proof is learned from the mishna alone I would say that during the second Jubilee cycle the owner is considered like another person. Therefore, the baraita teaches us that according to Rabbi Eliezer the owner is not considered like another person, and the field returns to him as an ancestral possession.

notes.he: קמ"ל ברייתא דלאו כאחר דמו:
notes.en: If from the mishna, I would have said, etc.: the baraita teaches us that they are not like another.

messages.text: Mishna

One who purchases an ancestral field from his father, and his father subsequently died and afterward the son consecrated it, its halakhic status is like that of an ancestral field, as he inherited his father’s ancestral rights prior to the consecration. Consequently, the field’s redemption price is calculated on the basis of fifty sela per beit kor, and if another redeems it instead of the son, it is given to the priests during the Jubilee Year.

notes.dh: מתני' הלוקח שדה מאביו ומת אביו כו' הרי היא כשדה אחוזה
notes.he: שהרי עד שלא הקדישה נפלה לו בירושה הלכך אם בא לפדותה פודה בית כור בנ' סלעים כשדה אחוזה ואם לא גאלה הוא וגאלה אחר יוצאה לכהנים ביובל:
notes.en: Mishna. One who purchases a field from his father and his father died, etc., it is like an ancestral field: since before he consecrated it, it fell to him by inheritance. Therefore, if he comes to redeem it, he redeems [it at] fifty sela per beit kor, like an ancestral field; and if he did not redeem it and another redeemed it, it goes out to the priests at the Jubilee.

messages.text: But if the son consecrated the field and afterward his father died, its halakhic status is like that of a purchased field, whose redemption price is based on its monetary value, and which will return to the ancestral owner, i.e., the son, at the Jubilee; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: דבתר שעה שהקדישה אזלינן הלכך אם בא לפדותה פודה בשווייה כדין שדה מקנה ואם לא גאלה הוא וגאלה אחר חוזרת לו ביובל שהרי בשעה שהקדישה לא היה גופה שלו דעתידה היא לחזור לאביו ביובל כדין שאר מכירות וכשאר מקדיש שדה מקנה הוא שהגואלה מיד גזבר מחזירה ביובל לאשר לו אחוזת הארץ דהיינו אביו וזה יורש את כח אביו:
notes.en: Like a purchased field: for we go by the time when he consecrated it. Therefore, if he comes to redeem it, he redeems it at its value, according to the law of a purchased field; and if he did not redeem it and another redeemed it, it returns to him at the Jubilee, since at the time he consecrated it the land itself was not his, as it was due to return to his father at the Jubilee like other sales. And he is like anyone else who consecrates a purchased field: whoever redeems it from the treasurer returns it at the Jubilee “to the one to whom the possession of the land belongs,” that is, his father, and this one inherits his father’s right.

messages.text: Even in a case where the son consecrated the field before his father died, its halakhic status is like that of an ancestral field, as it is stated with regard to a purchased field: “And if he will consecrate unto the Lord a field that he has bought, which is not of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:22), indicating that this halakha applies only to a field that is not due to become his ancestral field, thereby excluding this field, which at the time of consecration is due to become his ancestral field in the future, when his father dies.

verse.he: וְאִם אֶת־שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If one consecrates to GOD land that was purchased, which is not one’s land-holding,

notes.dh: יצאת זו שהיא ראויה להיות שדה אחוזה
notes.he: שכיון שאילו לא קנאה היתה נופלת לפניו בירושה והויא שדה אחוזה השתא נמי דאע"ג דהקדישה ואח"כ מת אביו הויא שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: Excluding this, which is fit to become an ancestral field: for since, had he not bought it, it would have fallen to him by inheritance and been an ancestral field, now too, even though he consecrated it and afterward his father died, it is an ancestral field.

messages.text: A purchased field that was consecrated is not removed from the possession of the Temple treasury and given to the priests during the Jubilee Year, as the purchase of the land was valid only until the Jubilee, at which point fields return to their ancestral owners, and a person cannot consecrate an item that is not his.

notes.he: שהקדישה וגאלה אחר אינה יוצאה לכהנים ביובל אלא למי שמכרה למקדישה:
notes.en: A purchased field: that one consecrated and another redeemed does not go out to the priests at the Jubilee, but [returns] to the one who sold it to the one who consecrated it.

notes.dh: שאין אדם מקדיש דבר שאינו שלו
notes.he: וקרקע זו לא היתה שלו אלא עד היובל:
notes.en: For a person cannot consecrate an item that is not his: and this land was his only until the Jubilee.

notes.dh: שדה מקנה אינה יוצאה לכהנים ביובל
notes.he: שאין אדם מקדיש דבר שאינו שלו לפום ריהטא משמע אם גאל האחר מהגזבר לפני היובל ורש"י פירש בפירוש חומש שלו דאפי' לא גאלה אחר אלא שעדיין היא ביד הגזבר תצא בחנם ביובל לבעלים הראשונים אשר לו אחוזת הארץ:
notes.en: A purchased field does not go out to the priests at the Jubilee, for a person cannot consecrate an item that is not his: At first glance it implies [that this is] where another redeemed it from the treasurer before the Jubilee. And Rashi explained in his commentary on the Torah that even if another did not redeem it, but it is still in the hand of the treasurer, it goes out for free at the Jubilee to the original owners, “to whom the possession of the land belongs.”

notes.dh: המקדיש שדה מקנה ולא גאלה אינה יוצאה לכהנים ביובל שאין אדם מקדיש דבר שאינו שלו
notes.he: שהיא אחוזתו של מוכר וחוזרת לו ביובל:
notes.en: One who consecrates a purchased field and did not redeem it, it does not go out to the priests at the Jubilee, for a person cannot consecrate an item that is not his: for it is the seller’s ancestral possession, and it returns to him at the Jubilee.

messages.text: The priests and the Levites may always consecrate their ancestral fields and may always redeem their ancestral fields, both before the Jubilee Year and after the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: מפרש בגמ':
notes.en: May always consecrate: this is explained in the Gemara.

notes.he: אם הקדיש כהן קרקע ירושתו גואלה אפי' לאחר היובל דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ה:ל״ב) גאולת עולם תהיה ללוים:
notes.en: And may always redeem: if a priest consecrated the land of his inheritance, he may redeem it even after the Jubilee, as it is written: “The Levites shall have a perpetual right of redemption” (Leviticus 25:32).

messages.text: Gemara

From where is it derived that one who purchases an ancestral field from his father and consecrated it, and afterward his father died, from where is it derived that it shall be treated for him like an ancestral field? The verse states: “And if he will consecrate unto the Lord a field that he has bought, which is not of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:22), indicating that this halakha applies only to a field that is not due to become his ancestral field, thereby excluding this field that he purchased from his father, which at the time of consecration is due to become his ancestral field; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.

From where is it derived with regard to one who purchases an ancestral field from his father, and his father died and afterward he consecrated the field, from where is it derived that it shall be treated for him like an ancestral field? The verse states: “And if he will consecrate unto the Lord a field that he has bought, which is not of his ancestral field.” This teaches that a field that is not an ancestral field at the time of consecration is deemed a purchased field, thereby excluding this field, which is at this point an ancestral field. But by this reading, a field that at the time of consecration is merely due to become an ancestral field in the future is deemed a purchased field.

messages.caption: A field bought from one’s father and then consecrated: its status in the mishna’s two cases, and how each side reads “which is not of his ancestral field.”

messages.text: Let us say that they disagree about this: That Rabbi Meir, who requires a derivation from the verse to teach the halakha that if the son consecrates the field after his father’s death it is not treated as a purchased field, holds that acquisition of an item for its produce is tantamount to acquisition of the item itself.
messages.quote: excluding this field, which is at this point an ancestral field

notes.dh: גמ' רבי מאיר סבר קנין פירות
notes.he: שהיתה קנויה לו לבן בחיי אביו לפירות לאכול הפירות ולא לגופה שהרי עתיד לחזור ביובל כקנין הגוף דמי הלכך כי מת אביו עד שלא הקדישה אי לא אשמועינן קרא דתיהוי כשדה אחוזה ה"א לאו שדה אחוזה היא דבלאו מיתת אביו היתה קנויה לו הילכך איצטריך קרא להכי אבל הקדישה בעודה שדה מקנה ואח"כ מת אביו לא רביא לן קרא דתיהוי אחוזה אלא שדה מקנה היא:
notes.en: Gemara. Rabbi Meir holds that acquisition of the produce: that it was acquired by the son in his father’s lifetime for the produce, to eat the produce, and not for [the land] itself, since it was due to return at the Jubilee, is like acquisition of the land itself. Therefore, when his father died before he consecrated it, had the verse not taught us that it is like an ancestral field, I would have said it is not an ancestral field, since even without his father’s death it was acquired by him; therefore a verse was necessary for this. But if he consecrated it while it was still a purchased field and afterward his father died, the verse does not include it for us as an ancestral field; rather, it is a purchased field.

notes.he: רבי מאיר סבר קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי:
notes.en: Rabbi Meir holds that acquisition of the produce is like acquisition of the land itself.

messages.text: Accordingly, as the son owned the plot as a purchased field prior to his father’s death, his ownership remained unchanged when his father died. Therefore, the verse is required to teach that upon the father’s death the field’s status changes to that of an ancestral field.

notes.he: דהלוקח שדה מאביו אין לו בחיי אביו אלא הפירות ורבי מאיר סבר קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי הלכך כי הקדישה בחיי אביו הרי היא כשדה מקנה דכשם שהפירות שלו כך קנה הגוף ושוב אינה ראויה להיות שדה אחוזתו אלא דין שדה מקנה יש לה:
notes.en: For one who buys a field from his father has, in his father’s lifetime, only the produce, and Rabbi Meir holds that acquisition of the produce is like acquisition of the land itself. Therefore, when he consecrated it in his father’s lifetime, it is like a purchased field: just as the produce is his, so he acquired the land itself, and it is no longer fit to be his ancestral field; rather, it has the law of a purchased field.

messages.text: In contrast, let us say that Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon hold that acquisition of an item for its produce is not tantamount to acquisition of the item itself. Accordingly, his ownership of the field became absolute only upon his father’s death. Consequently, there is no need for a derivation from the verse for such a case, and the derivation is therefore applied to the case where the son consecrated the field before his father’s death.

notes.dh: ורבי יהודה ורבי שמעון סברי לאו כקנין הגוף דמי
notes.he: וכי מת אביו קודם שהקדישה הוא דקא ירית לה לגופה ושדה אחוזה היא והלכך להאי לא איצטריך קרא לרבויי דהא אחוזה גמורה היא שבחיי אביו לא היתה קנויה לו וכי אתא קרא להקדישה ואח"כ מת אביו דאע"ג דבשעת הקדש הואי שדה מקנה השתא דמת אביו קודם פדיון שדה אחוזה היא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon hold that it is not like acquisition of the land itself: and when his father died before he consecrated it, he inherits the land itself, and it is an ancestral field. Therefore a verse was not necessary to include this case, since it is a full ancestral field, for in his father’s lifetime it was not acquired by him. And the verse comes for [the case where] he consecrated it and afterward his father died: even though at the time of consecration it was a purchased field, now that his father died before the redemption, it is an ancestral field.

notes.he: קנין פירות לאו כקנין הגוף דמי. הלכך אמרי הרי היא כשדה אחוזה שראויה להיות שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon hold: acquisition of the produce is not like acquisition of the land itself. Therefore they say it is like an ancestral field, since it is fit to be an ancestral field.

messages.text: In general, according to Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehuda, acquisition of an item for its produce is tantamount to acquisition of the item itself. Consequently, they also require the derivation from the verse to teach that if the father died before the son consecrated the field, it is treated as an ancestral field and not as a purchased field.
messages.quote: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon hold that acquisition of an item for its produce is not tantamount

notes.he: ולמת אביו ואח"כ הקדישה נמי איצטריך קרא:
notes.en: Is like acquisition of the land itself: and so for [the case where] his father died and afterward he consecrated it, a verse is also necessary.

notes.dh: לרבי יהודה ור"ש קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמיא כו'
notes.he: פירשתי בהשולח (גיטין דף מח.):
notes.en: According to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, acquisition of the produce is like acquisition of the land itself, etc.: I explained it in [the chapter] HaSholei’aḥ (Gittin 48a).

notes.he: בעלמא בכל דוכתא במי שכתב כל נכסיו לבנו לאחר מותו שניהם אינם יכולין למכור כלומר לר' יהודה ור' שמעון קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי. והכא קרא. יתירא:
notes.en: In general: everywhere, with regard to one who wrote all his property over to his son [to take effect] after his death, [where] neither of them can sell; that is, according to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, acquisition of the produce is like acquisition of the land itself. And here [they derive it from] a superfluous verse.

messages.text: Continues on 27a: then how do Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon also apply the verse to a son who consecrated the field before his father died? They read the extra word “of” in “which is not of his ancestral field.”
